prompts.title: Enable Spring Virtual Threads Safely
prompts.whenToUse: Decide whether a Spring Boot service should run on Java virtual threads and, if so, enable them safely: JDK verdict, executor inventory, pool sizes and acquire timeouts from downstream capacity, semaphores or bulkheads per fragile downstream, virtual-thread-per-task executors with CPU work kept on platform threads, context propagation across @Async, pinning fixes only where they matter, and an off-versus-on load-test plan with a minimal diff.
prompts.formatNotes: All three. Point the tool at the build file, Dockerfile or base image (runtime JDK), `application.yml`/`application.properties` (`spring.threads.virtual.enabled`, `server.tomcat.threads.*`, `spring.datasource.hikari.*`, `spring.task.*`), every executor and async configuration class, and the HTTP client config. Copilot: java-virtual-threads path instructions plus those files in agent mode. Claude Code: the java-virtual-threads-spring-guardrails skill plus the config files. Codex: AGENTS.md concurrency section, then the diff.
prompts.body:
Task: Decide whether the Spring Boot service I specify should run on Java virtual threads, and if so, enable them safely. Replace the old thread-pool ceiling with explicit limits on every finite resource, keep request context working across async hops, fix only the pinning that matters on our JDK, and finish with a minimal diff plus a load-test plan that compares off and on.

Context placeholders (fill from the repo or ask only if missing):
- Service root / module: {{APP_PATH}}
- JDK version (build and runtime image): {{JDK_VERSION}}  (21 | 24 | 25 | other)
- Spring Boot version: {{BOOT_VERSION}}  (e.g. 3.4, 3.5, 4.0, 4.1)
- Web stack: {{STACK}}  (Spring MVC servlet | WebFlux | both)
- Finite resources: {{POOLS}}  (e.g. Hikari 10, Apache HttpClient 20 per route, Redis Lettuce, Kafka producer)
- Downstream limits: {{DOWNSTREAM_LIMITS}}  (name → max concurrency or rate limit, or unknown)
- Custom executors: {{EXECUTORS}}  (bean names and purpose, or "find them")
- Context that must propagate: {{CONTEXT}}  (SecurityContext | MDC correlation ID | trace | tenant)
- Current symptom: {{SYMPTOM}}  (thread exhaustion | high latency under load | pool pending spikes after enabling | none, evaluating)
- Load-test tool and target: {{LOAD_TEST}}  (Gatling | k6 | JMeter | none yet; target RPS and p99)

Requirements:

1. Inventory
   - Read the build file, Dockerfile or base image (actual runtime JDK), and `application*.yml|properties` (`spring.threads.virtual.enabled`, `server.tomcat.threads.*`, `spring.datasource.hikari.*`, HTTP client pool settings, `spring.task.*`)
   - List every executor: auto-configured (`applicationTaskExecutor`, task scheduler, listener containers) and custom `TaskExecutor` / `ExecutorService` beans, with what runs on each and whether it is I/O or CPU bound
   - List every finite pool with size and acquire timeout, every `ThreadLocal` use, and every `synchronized` block or method that wraps blocking I/O
   - Note whether {{STACK}} is servlet or reactive and whether any reactive code blocks

2. Decision
   - State whether the service is I/O bound and thread-limited, with evidence (thread dumps, Tomcat busy threads, latency vs load). If it is CPU bound or a non-blocking WebFlux app, recommend not enabling and stop after the findings
   - State the JDK verdict: 24+ (no `synchronized` pinning) or 21 to 23 (pinning audit required); recommend JDK 25 if the base image allows

3. Findings (rank by risk: pools with no acquire timeout or sized below expected concurrency > unbounded fan-out or missing downstream limits > missing timeouts on blocking calls > pooled virtual threads or custom executors assumed to move > pinning on hot I/O paths (JDK 21 to 23 only) > ThreadLocal caches and lost context > CPU-bound work on request threads > observability gaps)

4. Fix
   - Enable `spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true` per environment (profile or ConfigMap), keeping the rollback a single property
   - Size each pool in {{POOLS}} from the database or downstream capacity in {{DOWNSTREAM_LIMITS}}; set Hikari `connection-timeout` and HTTP pending-acquire timeouts so waits fail fast
   - Add a `Semaphore` or Resilience4j bulkhead per fragile downstream; no fixed pools of virtual threads
   - Move blocking custom executors to virtual-thread-per-task (`SimpleAsyncTaskExecutor` with virtual threads and an optional concurrency limit); keep CPU-bound executors on a bounded platform pool
   - Propagate {{CONTEXT}} with a `TaskDecorator` or Micrometer context propagation; replace `ThreadLocal` caches with shared immutable objects or explicit parameters
   - On JDK 21 to 23 only: change `synchronized` to `ReentrantLock` (with `unlock()` in `finally`) where the lock is held across blocking I/O on a hot path; on 24+ leave `synchronized` alone
   - Bound any per-request fan-out and pass the remaining deadline to each child; cancel children when the parent fails
   - Keep or add timeouts on every JDBC query, HTTP call, lock wait, and queue poll

5. Tests
   - `@Async` and fan-out test proving SecurityContext, MDC correlation ID, and trace ID survive the hop
   - Concurrency test that fires more requests than the pool size and asserts acquire timeouts fail fast with a clear error instead of hanging
   - Bulkhead or semaphore test showing excess calls are rejected or queued as designed
   - A startup check or test that fails if the runtime JDK is below the stated floor

6. Load-test plan and verification
   - Off-versus-on comparison with {{LOAD_TEST}} at the same pool sizes: throughput, p95, p99, error rate, `hikaricp.connections.pending` and acquire time, HTTP pool pending, heap and GC, and JFR `jdk.VirtualThreadPinned` events (threshold about 20 ms)
   - Resource table: resource | size | acquire timeout | downstream capacity | limiter in front
   - Executor table: executor | before | after | I/O or CPU | concurrency limit
   - Alerts to add: pool pending and acquire time, bulkhead rejections, heap pressure, p99 latency

Constraints:
- Minimal diff. Don't rewrite working concurrency code that isn't on a hot blocking path.
- Don't invent pool sizes, downstream limits, or load numbers. Use placeholders and state assumptions.
- Don't add a reactive stack or a new concurrency library to "help" virtual threads.
- Optimize for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex: give concrete diffs and a checklist.
- Leave JDK base-image upgrades and alert rule changes as follow-up notes unless the repo already manages them.

Output format:
1. Decision (enable or not, and why) and JDK verdict
2. Findings table: severity | location | issue | fix
3. Patch (properties + pool limits + limiters + executor changes + context propagation + pinning fixes)
4. Tests added and their results
5. Resource and executor tables, load-test plan, and follow-ups

Start from {{APP_PATH}}. Bound the pools and downstreams before turning the property on.

prompts.title: Harden an LLM Feature Against Prompt Injection
prompts.whenToUse: Harden a chat, RAG, or tool-calling LLM feature against direct and indirect prompt injection, excessive tool agency, and unsafe output handling: inventory and trust map, ranked findings, retrieval filtered by caller access, tools in the caller's identity with validated arguments, code-enforced approval, loop and budget caps, output encoding per sink, guards and redacted logging, plus a red-team eval set wired into CI with before/after attack success rates.
prompts.formatNotes: All three. Point the tool at the prompt templates, the classes that build chat requests (Spring AI `ChatClient` and advisors, LangChain4j AI services, or SDK calls), every tool or function definition, the retrieval and vector-store query code, the code that renders or stores model output, and any eval folder. Copilot: llm-app-security path instructions plus those files in agent mode. Claude Code: the llm-app-prompt-injection-guardrails skill plus the files. Codex: AGENTS.md LLM section, then the diff.
prompts.body:
Task: Harden the LLM feature I specify against prompt injection (direct and indirect), excessive tool agency, and unsafe output handling. Map what the model reads and what it can do, close the paths from untrusted content to tools and output sinks in code, and finish with a minimal diff plus a red-team eval set that runs in CI.

Context placeholders (fill from the repo or ask only if missing):
- Feature / module root: {{APP_PATH}}
- Feature type: {{FEATURE}}  (chat | RAG Q&A | summarizer | tool-calling agent | LLM gateway | other)
- LLM stack: {{STACK}}  (Spring AI | LangChain4j | Azure OpenAI / OpenAI SDK | OpenAI-compatible router | other)
- Untrusted sources: {{SOURCES}}  (e.g. uploaded files, wiki pages, support tickets, emails, web pages, tool results)
- Tools exposed to the model: {{TOOLS}}  (name → what it reads or writes, or "find them")
- Tool identity today: {{TOOL_IDENTITY}}  (end-user on-behalf-of token | service principal / managed identity | API key | mixed)
- Output sinks: {{SINKS}}  (web UI Markdown/HTML | DB write | email or chat message | another service | shell or SQL)
- Tenancy and access model: {{TENANCY}}  (single tenant | multi-tenant with tenant ID from token | document ACLs)
- Guard services available: {{GUARDS}}  (e.g. Azure AI Content Safety Prompt Shields, PII detector, none)
- Eval runner: {{EVAL_RUNNER}}  (JUnit tests | promptfoo | custom harness | none yet)

Requirements:

1. Inventory
   - List every LLM call site in {{APP_PATH}}: prompt template and version, model and provider, the messages it builds (system, user, tool) and what goes into each
   - List every tool or function with its schema, what it reads or writes, the identity it runs as, and whether it can send data outside the tenant
   - List where each model output goes and how it is rendered, parsed, or executed
   - Note what is logged per call (raw prompts, completions, tool arguments) and where

2. Trust map
   - Mark every prompt input as trusted (code-built), user (signed-in caller), or untrusted (third-party content, tool output, other agents)
   - Draw each path from an untrusted source to a tool or an output sink; these paths are the attack surface

3. Findings (rank by risk: untrusted content reaching a write or outbound tool without approval > tools running with an identity broader than the caller > retrieval not filtered by the caller's access > model output reaching HTML, SQL, shell, file path, or URL sinks unencoded > generic tools such as fetch-any-URL, raw SQL, or exec > secrets, internal endpoints, or authorization logic in the system prompt > unbounded agent loops or budgets > missing guards > raw prompts and customer data in logs > no red-team evals)

4. Fix (code first, prompt wording last)
   - Move untrusted content out of the system message into its own delimited user or tool message, strip delimiter look-alikes from the content, and add one short rule that delimited content is data, not instructions
   - Remove secrets, internal URLs, and authorization logic from system prompts; enforce those rules in code
   - Filter retrieval by the caller's tenant and document ACLs before prompting
   - Switch tools to the caller's identity (on-behalf-of token or row-level filter); take tenant and user IDs from the authenticated principal, never from model arguments
   - Narrow tool schemas (enums, IDs, bounded strings), validate every argument server-side with authorization checks, host and path allow-lists, size limits, and idempotency keys for writes; replace generic fetch, SQL, or exec tools with specific ones
   - Add a code-enforced approval step (pending action plus explicit user confirmation showing exact arguments) for sends, deletes, bulk edits, permission changes, and payments
   - Cap tool rounds, total tokens or cost, and wall-clock time per request; abort on repeated identical tool calls
   - Encode output for each sink in {{SINKS}}: sanitized Markdown with raw HTML off, remote images disabled or proxied through an allow-list, strict CSP; use structured output with strict parsing where output drives code; never build SQL, shell commands, paths, or URLs from output by concatenation
   - Wire {{GUARDS}} on user input and retrieved documents, and PII or secret detection on output; log verdicts
   - Replace raw prompt logging with request ID, user, tenant, template version, document IDs, redacted tool arguments, guard verdicts, and token counts

5. Red-team evals
   - Direct injection in user input (override instructions, role-play, encoding tricks)
   - Indirect injection planted in a retrieved document and in a tool result, asking the model to call a tool or leak data
   - System-prompt extraction attempts
   - Cross-tenant or other-user data requests
   - Tool abuse: out-of-scope arguments, other tenant IDs, disallowed hosts, oversized inputs, repeated calls
   - Output-sink payloads: script tags, Markdown image exfiltration URLs, SQL and shell metacharacters
   - Each case asserts behaviour (no tool call, tool call rejected, output encoded, refusal, no foreign data), not exact wording; wire them into {{EVAL_RUNNER}} so CI fails on any new successful attack

6. Verification
   - Run the eval set before and after and report attack success rate per category
   - Run the normal-task eval or test suite to confirm answer quality and latency didn't regress
   - Tool table: tool | reads or writes | identity before | identity after | validation added | approval needed
   - Sink table: sink | before | encoding or parsing after

Constraints:
- Minimal diff. Don't rewrite prompts or features that aren't on an untrusted-to-tool or untrusted-to-sink path.
- Don't treat a keyword blocklist or a stronger system prompt as the fix for any finding.
- Don't invent guard services, tenant models, or eval scores. Use placeholders and state assumptions.
- Don't log real prompts, completions, or customer data in tests or examples.
- Optimize for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex: give concrete diffs and a checklist.
- Leave model or provider changes and new guard service rollouts as follow-up notes unless the repo already uses them.

Output format:
1. Trust map (sources → prompt messages → tools and sinks) with the attack-surface paths
2. Findings table: severity | location | issue | fix
3. Patch (message separation + retrieval filtering + tool identity and validation + approval step + loop limits + output encoding + guards + logging)
4. Red-team eval cases added and before/after attack success rate per category
5. Tool and sink tables, plus follow-ups

Start from {{APP_PATH}}. Close the paths from untrusted content to tools and sinks before touching prompt wording.

prompts.title: Evaluate RAG Retrieval & Grounding Quality
prompts.whenToUse: Measure whether a RAG feature retrieves the right evidence and answers only from it: golden questions with document-level relevance labels, retrieval-only recall@k, MRR, and nDCG, claim-level faithfulness, citation validity, correct- and false-refusal rates, judge calibration against human labels, per-query latency and cost, a paired comparison for a chunking, embedding, re-ranker, prompt, or model change, stage-tagged failures, and CI regression thresholds with a leakage check.
prompts.formatNotes: All three. Point the tool at the ingest and chunking code, the embedding and vector-store or search client, the retriever and re-ranker, the prompt template and the class that builds the chat request with citations, the eval folder and golden set, and the CI workflow. Copilot: rag-eval path instructions plus those files in agent mode (or save it as `.github/prompts/evaluate-rag-retrieval-quality.prompt.md`). Claude Code: the rag-retrieval-eval-guardrails skill plus the files. Codex: AGENTS.md RAG evals section, then the diff.
prompts.body:
Task: Evaluate the retrieval and grounding quality of the RAG feature I specify. Build or audit a golden question set with labelled evidence, score the retriever on its own, score answers for faithfulness, citation correctness, and refusal when evidence is missing, calibrate any LLM judge against human labels, and finish with a minimal diff that runs these evals in CI with regression thresholds.

Context placeholders (fill from the repo or ask only if missing):
- RAG module root: {{APP_PATH}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}  (Spring AI | LangChain4j | LlamaIndex | LangChain | custom)
- Retriever: {{RETRIEVER}}  (vector store and distance metric | keyword search | hybrid; plus re-ranker or none)
- Chunking and embedding today: {{CHUNKING}}  (splitter, chunk size, overlap; embedding model and dimensions)
- Top-k used in the prompt: {{TOP_K}}
- Corpus snapshot: {{CORPUS}}  (where it lives and how it is versioned)
- Golden set: {{GOLDEN}}  (e.g. evals/rag/golden.jsonl, or "none yet")
- Change under test: {{CHANGE}}  (e.g. chunk 512→1024, new embedding model, add re-ranker, new prompt, new model, or "baseline only")
- Judge model: {{JUDGE}}  (pinned version, or none)
- Eval runner and CI: {{EVAL_RUNNER}}  (pytest | JUnit | Ragas or similar library | custom harness; GitHub Actions | Jenkins)
- Budgets: {{BUDGETS}}  (e.g. p95 latency ≤ 2.5 s, cost per query ≤ $0.004)

Requirements:

1. Inventory
   - Document the pipeline in {{APP_PATH}}: loaders, splitter and chunk settings, embedding model, index and filters, hybrid weights, {{TOP_K}}, re-ranker, prompt template and version, model, and where citations and refusals are produced
   - List existing eval code, data, and metrics, and note anything unpinned (model aliases, corpus not versioned, judge unpinned)
   - Flag any golden or fixture data that contains real customer data or PHI

2. Golden set
   - Each case: stable `id`, `question`, `relevant_ids` as stable document IDs plus span or required facts (graded 0–3 if possible), short reference answer or required facts, and tags (lookup, multi-hop, comparison, numeric, recent-change, no-answer, ambiguous, past-incident)
   - At least 10% `no-answer` cases whose answer is not in {{CORPUS}}
   - A frozen held-out slice that is not used for tuning
   - Map document-level labels onto current chunks at eval time so a chunking change doesn't break labels
   - If {{GOLDEN}} is missing, propose 30 starter cases from the corpus and mark them for human review; drop synthetic questions that copy chunk text nearly verbatim
   - Don't rewrite or delete existing cases; flag questionable ones in the report

3. Retrieval metrics (retriever only, no LLM)
   - recall@k, MRR, and nDCG@k at {{TOP_K}} (and at 2×{{TOP_K}} to show headroom), context precision at k, and retrieved-context tokens, overall and per tag

4. Generation metrics (end to end)
   - Claim-level faithfulness against retrieved context only: supported-claim share and the count of answers with any unsupported claim
   - Citation validity (every cited ID was in the prompt for that request, checked in code), citation precision, and citation recall
   - Correct-refusal rate on no-answer cases and on cases with forced irrelevant context; false-refusal rate on answerable cases
   - Answer correctness against the reference or required facts
   - Per-query retrieval, re-rank, and generation latency (p50/p95), prompt, completion, and context tokens, and cost

5. Judge calibration (only if a judge is used)
   - Hand-label 100–200 answers with a written binary rubric per claim, split dev and held-out
   - Report judge precision, recall, and Cohen's kappa on held-out labels; pin judge model, prompt, temperature, and parser
   - Keep judge metrics warn-only until agreement is acceptable; the model under test never judges itself

6. Compare {{CHANGE}}
   - Same golden set, same corpus snapshot, same {{TOP_K}} unless top-k is the change; full re-embed for embedding changes
   - Paired per-case comparison against the current configuration, per tag, with token, latency, and cost deltas
   - Stage-tag every failure: not retrieved, ranked below k, in context but ignored, unsupported claim, wrong citation, should have refused

7. CI gate
   - Commit the accepted run as a baseline (separate commit, with the pins it came from)
   - Per-metric floor and tolerance: recall@k, MRR, faithfulness, citation validity, correct-refusal rate; budgets from {{BUDGETS}} for p95 latency and cost per query
   - Deterministic retrieval and citation-validity metrics block now; calibrated judge metrics block once step 5 passes
   - Path-filter the job on retrieval, ingest, prompt, model config, and eval code; write a results file with pins and a short Markdown summary; exit non-zero on regression

8. Leakage checks
   - Confirm no golden question or reference answer appears in prompts, few-shot examples, fine-tuning data, or re-ranker or embedder training data; add a test that fails if one does

Constraints:
- Minimal diff. Don't change retrieval or prompt behaviour unless {{CHANGE}} asks for it; report findings instead.
- Don't edit the golden set, labels, or baseline in the same commit as a retrieval, prompt, or model change.
- Don't invent scores, labels, or corpus contents. Use placeholders and state assumptions.
- Don't put real customer data, PHI, or secrets in fixtures, logs, or reports.
- Optimize for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex: give concrete diffs and a checklist.
- Leave index migrations and model swaps as follow-up notes unless they are {{CHANGE}}.

Output format:
1. Pipeline summary with pins and unpinned items
2. Golden set report: case counts per tag, no-answer share, held-out size, flagged cases
3. Metrics table: metric | baseline | candidate | delta | per-tag notes (retrieval, generation, refusal, cost, latency)
4. Judge calibration table (if used): metric | precision | recall | kappa | blocking yes/no
5. Stage-tagged failure table: case id | stage | evidence | suggested fix
6. Patch (eval harness, metrics, gate config, CI wiring, leakage test) plus follow-ups

Start from {{APP_PATH}}. Score the retriever on its own before judging any answer.

prompts.title: Add LLM Token Budgets & Cost Tracking
prompts.whenToUse: Meter, price, and bound the LLM calls in a service or gateway: inventory every model call, read token usage from provider responses (including streams), price it from a versioned table, attribute it to route, caller, and resolved model, add max-token, context, and agent-step caps, per-caller and global budgets with reserve-then-reconcile and a report-only mode, retry accounting, staged latency histograms, a cost report, and tests.
prompts.formatNotes: All three. Point the tool at the model client or gateway code, the retry and fallback config, the application config with model aliases, the auth or caller-identity code, and the metrics setup. Copilot: llm-cost path instructions plus those files in agent mode (or save it as `.github/prompts/add-llm-token-budgets-and-cost-tracking.prompt.md`). Claude Code: the llm-cost-latency-budget-guardrails skill plus the files. Codex: AGENTS.md LLM cost and latency section, then the diff.
prompts.body:
Task: Add token budgets, cost tracking, and latency measurement to the LLM calls in the service I specify. Inventory every model call, meter usage from provider responses, price it from a versioned table, cap each request, add caller and global budgets, fix retry accounting, and finish with a minimal diff, tests, and a cost report.

Context placeholders (fill from the repo or ask only if missing):
- Service or module root: {{APP_PATH}}
- Stack: {{STACK}}  (Spring Boot + Spring AI | LangChain4j | plain HTTP client | Python SDK | gateway)
- Providers and models: {{PROVIDERS}}  (e.g. Azure OpenAI deployments, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, OpenRouter, Anthropic)
- Callers to attribute: {{CALLERS}}  (service, tenant, user, or feature; and where the identity comes from)
- Price source: {{PRICES}}  (list prices with date, or negotiated rates; currency)
- Budgets: {{BUDGETS}}  (e.g. 200k tokens per caller per day, $50 global per day, max 8 agent steps)
- Latency SLO: {{SLO}}  (e.g. p95 time to first token ≤ 1.5 s, p95 total ≤ 8 s)
- Usage store and metrics: {{STORE}}  (database table, append-only log, Micrometer/OpenTelemetry metrics backend)
- Mode: {{MODE}}  (report-only | enforce)

Requirements:

1. Inventory
   - Table of every model call in {{APP_PATH}}: file and method, route or feature, caller, model alias, max output tokens (or "not set"), streaming, tools or agent loop, retry and fallback policy
   - Flag calls with no max output tokens, streams that never read usage, agent loops with no step cap, and retries of non-retryable errors

2. Metering
   - One usage hook (client interceptor, gateway filter, or callback), not per-call code
   - Read provider usage: input, output, and, where reported, cached-input and reasoning tokens; for OpenAI-compatible streams request the final usage chunk and count streams that end without it
   - Record: request ID, trace ID, route, caller ID (stable ID, never an email), requested alias, resolved provider and model version, attempt number, outcome, token counts, timings, cost, price table version
   - Never store prompts or completions in the usage store; redact them in logs

3. Pricing
   - Versioned price table from {{PRICES}} keyed by provider, model, and token type, with effective date and currency
   - Cost computed at write time; unit tests for every token type and for a model missing from the table (record it, flag it, don't price it as zero)

4. Request caps
   - Explicit max output tokens per route, input and retrieved-context caps, tool-result size cap, agent step and total-token cap per run
   - A clear error or trim policy when a cap is hit; a CI or unit check that fails when a route has no max output tokens

5. Budgets
   - Per-caller per-window and global daily budgets from {{BUDGETS}}
   - Reserve an estimate before the call, reconcile with actual usage after it, release on failure; safe under concurrency
   - Blocked response: documented status (e.g. 429 with reason and Retry-After) and a metric; in report-only {{MODE}}, log and count would-be blocks without rejecting
   - Alert at a threshold below the global ceiling and on sudden jumps in tokens per request

6. Retries and fallbacks
   - Retry only timeouts, 429, and 5xx, with capped exponential backoff and jitter, honouring Retry-After, with a total attempt and time limit
   - Every attempt's tokens count against the caller's budget; record which provider and model each attempt used
   - Cancel the upstream call when the client disconnects

7. Latency
   - Histograms for total duration, time to first token, output tokens per second, gateway overhead, and retry wait, tagged by route, provider, model, and outcome
   - Labels stay low-cardinality: no user IDs, request IDs, or prompt text; if using OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions, pin the version
   - Report against {{SLO}}

8. Report and tests
   - A query or endpoint that reports cost, tokens, p95 latency, and error rate per day, route, caller, and model from {{STORE}}
   - Tests: pricing, reserve-and-reconcile under concurrency, streaming with and without final usage, retry accounting, blocked response, missing-price handling

Constraints:

prompts.body:
Task: Add signed build provenance and SBOM attestations to the release pipeline for the artifacts I specify, verify them with an exact identity before every deploy, and stage admission enforcement on AKS. Finish with a minimal diff, a verification runbook, and negative tests.

Context placeholders (fill from the repo or ask only if missing):
- Artifacts: {{ARTIFACTS}}  (e.g. container image app-api, Spring Boot JAR, CLI binary)
- Registries: {{REGISTRIES}}  (e.g. dev ACR and prod ACR, or GHCR)
- Release workflow: {{RELEASE_WORKFLOW}}  (e.g. .github/workflows/release.yml; trigger such as tag v* or push to main)
- Deploy path: {{DEPLOY}}  (e.g. GitHub Actions deploy job with Kustomize overlay, or GitOps repo)
- Repo visibility and plan: {{VISIBILITY}}  (public, or private on GitHub Enterprise Cloud)
- Runners: {{RUNNERS}}  (GitHub-hosted or self-hosted)
- Target SLSA build level: {{SLSA_LEVEL}}  (L2 or L3)
- SBOM format and tool: {{SBOM}}  (e.g. CycloneDX via syft, or the CycloneDX Maven plugin)
- Admission option: {{ADMISSION}}  (Kyverno verifyImages, Ratify with Gatekeeper and Azure Policy, or none yet)
- Signing requirement: {{SIGNING}}  (keyless via actions/attest, or Notation with a Key Vault certificate)

Requirements:

1. Map the current state
   - Table: artifact | built by (workflow/job) | pushed to | how deploy selects it (tag or digest) | signed or attested today | verified where
   - Flag mutable-tag deploys, stored signing keys, broad workflow permissions, unpinned actions, and attestations from untrusted triggers

2. Attest
   - Capture the digest from the build step output; attest `name@digest`, never a tag
   - Add `actions/attest` (SHA-pinned) for provenance and a second call with `sbom-path` for the SBOM, both with `push-to-registry: true`
   - Job-level permissions only on the attest job: `id-token: write`, `attestations: write`, `artifact-metadata: write`, plus registry write (`packages: write` for GHCR, or OIDC login with AcrPush for ACR)
   - No attestation on pull_request, fork, or `pull_request_target` runs
   - If {{SIGNING}} is Notation: sign through the Azure Key Vault plugin after OIDC login; no key material in secrets

3. Builder isolation for {{SLSA_LEVEL}}
   - L2: GitHub-hosted runners and the steps above
   - L3: move build and attest into a reusable workflow that callers can't modify; callers pass inputs only
   - Say plainly which level the result supports and why; don't overclaim with self-hosted runners

4. Verify before deploy
   - In {{DEPLOY}}: `gh attestation verify oci://<image>@<digest> --repo <owner>/<repo> --signer-workflow <path> --source-ref <ref>`; add `--deny-self-hosted-runners` when builds are hosted; verify the SBOM attestation with `--predicate-type`
   - Fail closed: no retry loop, no skip input, no `continue-on-error`
   - Pass the verified digest into the manifest or overlay; the deployed spec must reference the digest
   - Private repos: document the trusted-root step for any verifier outside gh, and offline verification with `--bundle` if needed

5. Promotion
   - Promote by digest without rebuilding; copy referrers with the image (for example `oras cp -r`), or verify in the source and re-attest in the target
   - Re-verify in the target registry before the prod deploy

6. Admission on AKS ({{ADMISSION}})
   - Policy that checks signatures or attestations for {{REGISTRIES}} with an identity matching the release workflow
   - Ship in audit mode first; list how to read violations; enforce on app namespaces only after a clean audit window
   - Narrow, documented exemptions with owner and expiry; explicit webhook timeout and failure policy
   - Note that AKS Image Integrity is preview, Notation-only, and audit-only, if it is under consideration

7. Negative tests
   - An unsigned image, an image attested by a different workflow, and a tag swapped after verification: each must fail in the pipeline and be flagged or blocked at admission

Constraints:
- Minimal diff. Don't change build steps, tests, scanners, or app code beyond what attestation and verification need.
- Never add signing keys, tokens, or certificates to the repo or to plain secrets; never print OIDC tokens.
- Don't apply admission policies to a cluster. Provide the manifests and the commands for a non-production dry run.
- Don't invent registry names, workflow paths, digests, or tenant IDs; use placeholders and state assumptions.
- Treat provenance as origin proof only; keep CVE and license gates as they are.
- Optimize for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex: give concrete diffs and a checklist.

Output format:
1. Current-state table with flagged issues
2. Patch (release workflow, reusable workflow if L3, deploy verification step, promotion step, admission policy in audit mode)
3. Permission matrix per job
4. Verification runbook: exact commands for a developer, for CI, and for an incident responder checking a running pod's image
5. Negative test plan and expected results
6. Risks, SLSA level actually achieved, and follow-ups

Start from {{RELEASE_WORKFLOW}}. Capture the digest first, verify before you deploy, and audit before you enforce.

   - A small CI check that fails on literal tokens, populated Authorization headers, `@latest`, `enableAllProjectMcpServers`, and "*" tool lists in those files

8. Tests

- Don't connect to production systems or call write tools while testing; use a sandbox repo, project, or database.

prompts.whenToUse: Set up or clean up Dependabot or Renovate for a Maven or Gradle service with Dockerfiles and GitHub Actions: inventory coverage and pinning, group updates by risk with a separate Spring Boot group, schedule them with small PR limits, add release-age cooldowns, pin actions by SHA and images by digest, and allow auto-merge only for low-risk patch or minor updates behind required checks, with a test that proves a failing or high-risk update does not merge.

Point the tool at `.github/dependabot.yml` or the Renovate config, every `pom.xml` or `build.gradle(.kts)` and `gradle/libs.versions.toml`, the Dockerfiles, `.github/workflows/`, and CODEOWNERS, and paste the output of `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection` (or the ruleset) so required checks are known. Claude Code: the dependency-update-automation-guardrails skill plus the files. Codex: AGENTS.md dependency updates section, then the diff.
prompts.body:
Task: Configure grouped, scheduled dependency updates with release-age delays and a narrow, check-gated auto-merge for this repository. Cover Maven or Gradle, GitHub Actions, and Docker. Finish with a minimal diff, a grouping plan, and a test that proves a failing or high-risk update does not merge.

Context placeholders (fill from the repo or ask only if missing):
- Bot: {{BOT}}  (Dependabot, Renovate, or "recommend one"; one bot per ecosystem)
- Build: {{BUILD}}  (Maven with spring-boot-starter-parent, Maven with the spring-boot-dependencies BOM, or Gradle with version catalog and the Spring Boot plugin)
- Manifest locations: {{MANIFESTS}}  (e.g. /, /services/*, Dockerfiles in /docker and /services/*/)
- Other ecosystems: {{OTHER_ECOSYSTEMS}}  (docker-compose, helm, terraform, or none)
- Schedule and timezone: {{SCHEDULE}}  (e.g. weekly, Monday 09:00, Asia/Kolkata)
- Release-age delay: {{COOLDOWN}}  (e.g. 5 days patch/minor, 14 days for auto-merged and major)
- Auto-merge scope: {{AUTOMERGE_SCOPE}}  (e.g. patch and minor of Maven plugins, test libraries, GitHub Actions, image digests; or "none")
- Never auto-merge: {{NEVER_AUTOMERGE}}  (e.g. majors, Spring Boot minors, spring-security, nimbus-jose-jwt, jackson, JDBC drivers)
- Required checks on main: {{REQUIRED_CHECKS}}  (e.g. build, test, dependency-scan; or "unknown")
- Merge method and queue: {{MERGE_METHOD}}  (merge, squash, or rebase; merge queue yes or no)
- Private registries: {{REGISTRIES}}  (e.g. Azure Artifacts Maven feed, ACR; or none)

Requirements:

1. Inventory
   - Table: ecosystem | manifest paths | covered by (Dependabot, Renovate, none) | pinned (actions by SHA, images by digest, yes or no) | open bot PRs today | oldest open bot PR
   - Flag: ecosystems with no coverage, the same manifest covered by two bots, `@v4`-style or branch refs in `uses:`, `latest` or tag-only base images, managed-version overrides without a reason, literal registry credentials

2. Groups and schedule
   - Per ecosystem: a tooling and test group (patch and minor), a runtime library group (patch and minor), a Spring Boot group (`org.springframework.boot:*` plus the Boot Gradle plugin; Renovate `group:springBoot`), majors ungrouped
   - Security updates: own group with `applies-to: security-updates` (Dependabot) or default vulnerability handling (Renovate); never blocked by a version group
   - Order Dependabot groups from most specific to most general
   - {{SCHEDULE}} with explicit timezone; `open-pull-requests-limit` (Dependabot) or `prConcurrentLimit` and `prHourlyLimit` (Renovate) between 3 and 5
   - Use `directories` globs or Renovate defaults for {{MANIFESTS}}; `exclude-paths` for fixtures

3. Release-age delay
   - Dependabot: `cooldown` with `default-days` and semver-specific days from {{COOLDOWN}}; `exclude` for internal group IDs
   - Renovate: `minimumReleaseAge` per rule, `internalChecksFilter: "strict"`, `waitForAllUpdates: true` on groups
   - Longer delay for anything inside {{AUTOMERGE_SCOPE}}; state that security updates bypass it

4. Pinning
   - Separate commit: pin every `uses:` to a full commit SHA with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment; pin base images as `image:tag@sha256:<digest>`
   - Renovate: extend `config:best-practices` (or add `helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests` and `docker:pinDigests`)
   - Don't invent SHAs or digests: resolve them with `gh api repos/<owner>/<action>/commits/<tag> --jq .sha` and `docker buildx imagetools inspect <image>:<tag>`, or leave a placeholder and list it

5. Spring Boot
   - Let Boot and its BOM move managed libraries; list every existing override with its reason; propose removing the ones Boot already covers
   - Boot patch inside auto-merge only if {{AUTOMERGE_SCOPE}} says so and the test suite covers startup and integration; Boot minor and major never auto-merge
   - Gradle: keep the Boot plugin and `org.springframework.boot` platform in the same group

6. Auto-merge gate
   - Confirm {{REQUIRED_CHECKS}} via `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection` or the rulesets API; if none are required, stop and output the ruleset change instead of enabling auto-merge
   - Confirm repository "Allow auto-merge" is on (`gh repo view --json autoMergeAllowed`)
   - Dependabot: `.github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml` on `pull_request` only; `if` on `github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'dependabot[bot]'` and the repository name; job-level `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`; `dependabot/fetch-metadata` pinned by SHA; `gh pr merge --auto --{{MERGE_METHOD}}` only when `update-type` and `dependency-names` fall within {{AUTOMERGE_SCOPE}} and outside {{NEVER_AUTOMERGE}}; no checkout, no scripts, no secrets
   - Renovate: `packageRules` with `matchUpdateTypes`, `matchPackageNames` or `matchManagers`, `automerge: true`; explicit `automerge: false` rule for {{NEVER_AUTOMERGE}} placed after it
   - Merge queue: document that `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot enqueue and that a GitHub App token is needed

7. Registries and secrets
   - {{REGISTRIES}} as Dependabot `registries` with `${{secrets.NAME}}` or OIDC (`tenant-id`, `client-id`), or Renovate `hostRules` with encrypted values; list the Dependabot secrets to create, without values

8. Ownership and validation
   - CODEOWNERS for the bot config and the auto-merge workflow
   - CI step for Renovate: `npx --yes --package renovate -- renovate-config-validator --strict`
   - Majors ignored only with a comment and a tracking issue

9. Proof
   - Push a failing test to a patch-group branch: it must not merge
   - A major and a Spring Boot minor: no auto-merge, reviewers requested
   - A security update: opens even during cooldown and outside the schedule

Constraints:
- Minimal diff. Don't change application code, build plugins, or CI jobs beyond pinning and the auto-merge workflow.
- Never use `pull_request_target`, never check out PR code in the auto-merge job, and never grant workflow-level write permissions.
- Don't enable auto-merge on a branch without required checks.
- Don't invent SHAs, digests, group IDs, secret names, or check names; use placeholders and state assumptions.
- Optimize for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex: give concrete diffs and a checklist.

Output format:
1. Inventory table with flagged issues
2. Grouping plan: group | ecosystem | matches | update types | cooldown | auto-merge yes or no | why
3. Patch: bot config, pinning commit, auto-merge workflow or Renovate rules, CODEOWNERS, validator step
4. Branch protection or ruleset changes needed (as `gh api` commands to review, not to run)
5. Proof plan with expected results
6. Risks and follow-ups (e.g. overrides to remove, majors to plan)

Start with the inventory. Pin before you automate, and gate before you auto-merge.
